items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014
items.q: The interviewer mentions Ron Carter having a group at the Iridium; the interviewee responds by discussing the economics of jazz clubs and living costs, without indicating any personal interaction or professional relationship with Ron Carter.

ctx.x: Yeah it was a band that George Wein had. I think it might have been one of the last times we worked with him.

You know I think the last time I went to a club in New York, I think it was the Iridium. And Ron Carter had a group. It was very good but it was not his group, it was who can I get. But it cost me, this was probably ten years ago, it cost me I think almost $70, by the time I paid the cover and had a couple of drinks. And I’m wondering about two things. Like how does that kind of thing sustain itself, if we’re worried about our audience; and also what are those musicians getting paid?

Well it depends and that’s what I’m saying, that’s one of the difficult things now for jazz. And it’s not just jazz, it’s life period. Everything is so expensive. And who’s to be blamed? I’m not sure. I mean we all know somebody’s walking away with a bigger cut of the pie, you know, than it needs to be, where it makes it unfair. But it’s caused everything to go up to the point where the little people are getting squeezed out and screaming or complaining. Even these talks about minimum wage. I mean on the one hand…
